subject: Art & Design
title: Line Length: The 45-75 Character Rule
description: A short lesson to help you apply Line Length: The 45-75 Character Rule.

hook.text: Reading a line of text that stretches across your entire widescreen monitor feels exhausting. Here's why.

buildup.text: The eye has to travel back to the start of the next line. Longer lines = harder to find your place.

discovery.text: The ideal line length is 45-75 characters per line. Books, newspapers, and good websites all follow this.

twist.text: On mobile, shorter is better: 30-40 characters. That's why responsive design adjusts column width.

climax.text: Set max-width on text containers. Never let paragraphs stretch to the full viewport width.

punchline.text: The best text doesn't fill the screen. It respects the eye.

quiz.question: What is the ideal line length for body text?
options: As wide as the screen allows

details.summary: Optimal line length for comfortable reading is 45-75 characters per line (including spaces). Lines shorter than 45 characters create choppy, disjointed reading. Lines longer than 75 characters cause eye fatigue as readers struggle to track from line-end to the beginning of the next line.
details.whyItMatters: Line length directly affects reading comfort and comprehension. Too-wide columns are the most common typography error on the web, where responsive layouts can stretch text across entire screens. This simple rule prevents the problem.
takeaways: Optimal line length is 45-75 characters per line
Short lines chop reading flow; long lines cause eye fatigue
This is the most common typography error on the web

faq.question: How do you control line length in responsive web design?
faq.answer: Use max-width on text containers (typically 600-700px for body text) rather than letting text span the full viewport. The CSS 'ch' unit (character width) allows setting max-width directly in character counts: 'max-width: 65ch' ensures approximately 65 characters per line regardless of font size.

faq.question: Does the 45-75 rule apply to mobile screens?
faq.answer: Mobile screens naturally constrain line length, often falling within or below the ideal range. At typical mobile widths and body text sizes, lines are around 35-50 characters. This is slightly short but acceptable because mobile reading patterns involve quicker scanning and shorter attention spans.
